top_cited_works.title: Blowoff dynamics of bluff body stabilized turbulent premixed flames
Entrainment in the Near and Far Field of Fire Plumes
top_cited_works.abstract: This paper describes entrainment measurements made in fire plumes with a new technique. Measurements were in plumes rising from natural gas diffusion flames stabilized on 0.10, 0.19 and 0.50 m diameter burners and the heat release rates ranged from 10 to 200 kW. The heights examined ranged from elevations starting very close to the burner surface to distances about five times the average flame heights. Experiments indicate the presence of three regions: a region close to the burner surface where plume entrainment rates are independent of the fuel flow (or heat release) rates; a far field region above the flame top, where a simple point source model correlates the data reasonably well; and an intermediate region where entrainment appears to be similar to that of a turbulent plume.

recent_works.title: Impact of Effusion Hole Exit Geometry on the Cooling Performance of TBC Coated Surfaces in a High Temperature Combustion Environment
recent_works.abstract: Abstract This study examined the thermal characteristics and cooling performance of effusion cooling configurations by means of laser Rayleigh scattering (LRS) and infrared thermography. Combustor liners exposed to high temperature combustor flow in modern gas turbine engines are designed with advanced effusion cooling configurations to prevent damage and failure of the metal alloy. Thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) are applied to surfaces to reduce the thermal load on metal combustor liners. Effusion cooling hole geometries impact cooling performance and cooling film development. In this study, the impact of effusion jet hole blockage was investigated. An experimental test rig with a bulk vitiated crossflow of 1500K was used to study cooling performance of two effusion cooled plates: one with contracted effusion hole openings, and the other without. Carbon dioxide was used as the coolant over a range of blowing ratios (2.5–12) when the test rig reached quasi-steady operating conditions. Infrared imaging of the cooling array surface indicated higher temperatures for the contracted hole openings.
